source_text: Inter hos scopulos et sinus, inter haec uada et freta idololatriae uelificata spiritu dei fides nauigat, tuta si cauta, secura si attonita. ceterum inenatabile excussis profundum est, inextricabile inpactis naufragium est, inrespirabile deuoratis hypobrychium in idololatria. quicumque fluctus eius offocant, omnis uertex eius ad inferos desorbet. nemo dicat: quis tam tuto praecauebit? exeundum de saeculo erit. quasi non tanti sit exire, quam idololatren in saeculo stare. nihil esse facilius potest, quam cautio idololatriae, si timor eius in capite sit. quaecumque necessitas minor est periculo tanto comparata. propterea spiritus sanctus consultantibus tunc apostolis uinculum et iugum nobis relaxauit, ut idololatriae deuitandae uacaremus.. haec erit lex nostra, quo expedita hoc plenius administranda, propria Christianorum, per quam ab ethnicis agnoscimur et examinamur, haec accedentibus ad fidem proponenda et ingredientibus in fidem inculcanda est, ut accedentes deliberent, obseruantes perseuerent, non obseruantes renuntient sibi. uiderimus enim si secundum arcae typum et coruus et miluus et lupus et canis et serpens in ecclesia erit. certe idololatres in arcae typo non habetur. nullum animal in idololatren figuratum est. quod in arca non fuit, in ecclesia non sit.
thought_title: The ship of faith amid idolatry's reefs, and the ark's exclusion of idolaters
orientation: Tertullian is concluding the treatise by picturing the Christian's perilous course through idolatry and then applying the type of Noah's ark to the church.
pass_a_gloss: Among these rocks and bays, among these shallows and straits of idolatry, faith, sailed by the Spirit of God, navigates, safe if cautious, secure if thunderstruck. But for those who are shaken out, the deep is unswimmable; for those who are driven upon them, the shipwreck is inextricable; for those who are swallowed down, the drowning in idolatry is unbreathable. All its waves choke them; every whirlpool of it sucks them down to the dead. Let no one say: who will take precautions so safely? It will be necessary to go out of the world. As if going out were not worth as much as standing as an idolater in the world. Nothing can be easier than caution against idolatry, if the fear of it is at the head. Any necessity is smaller when compared with so great a danger. For this reason the Holy Spirit, when the apostles were then consulting, relaxed for us the bond and the yoke, so that we might be free to avoid idolatry. This will be our law, the more expedited, the more fully it is to be administered, proper to Christians, by which we are recognized and examined by pagans; this is to be set before those approaching the faith and to be pressed upon those entering the faith, so that those approaching may deliberate, those observing may persevere, those not observing may renounce themselves. For we shall see if, according to the type of the ark, the raven and the kite and the wolf and the dog and the serpent will be in the church. Certainly the idolater is not held in the type of the ark. No animal was figured as an idolater. What was not in the ark, let it not be in the church.

lemmas.gloss: will take precautions, will be on guard
to be pressed upon, to be impressed

choices.english: sailed by the Spirit of God
choices.why: Keeps the passive participle's force: faith is the ship, the Spirit is the wind that drives it; 'sailed by' preserves the agency.
rejected: with sails filled by the Spirit of God
driven by the Spirit of God

choices.why: The word means struck by thunder, hence awestruck; 'thunderstruck' keeps the literal image of being struck by divine awe, matching the nautical peril imagery.
The Greek loanword means submersion under water; 'drowning' gives the concrete sense of being swallowed down in idolatry.
The future perfect 'uiderimus' has the force of 'we shall see' or 'we will have seen'; rendering it as future keeps the rhetorical challenge.
rejected: For we will have seen if

choices.why: The passive 'figuratum est' means 'was represented as a type'; 'figured as' preserves the typological sense Tertullian is using for the ark.
rejected: was a figure of an idolater

choices.why: The dative 'sibi' with 'renuntio' means to renounce or disown oneself; keeping the reflexive dative preserves the stark demand.

pass_b_english: Among these rocks and bays, among these shallows and straits of idolatry, faith sails with the Spirit of God as its wind. It is safe if it is careful, secure if it is watchful. But for those who are thrown overboard, the deep cannot be crossed by swimming. For those who are driven onto the rocks, the shipwreck cannot be escaped. For those who are swallowed down, the drowning in idolatry leaves no breath. Every wave of idolatry chokes those it overwhelms, and every whirlpool of idolatry sucks them down to the underworld.

Let no one say, "Who can be on guard so carefully? We would have to leave the world." As if leaving the world were not worth as much as standing in the world as an idolater. Nothing can be easier than guarding against idolatry, if the fear of it stands first in the mind. Any necessity is small when compared with so great a danger. For this reason the Holy Spirit, when the apostles consulted Him at that time, loosened the bond and yoke for us, so that we might be free to devote ourselves to avoiding idolatry.

This will be our law. The more unencumbered it is, the more fully it must be administered. It is the law proper to Christians, by which we are recognized and tested among pagans. This law must be set before those who are coming to the faith and pressed upon those who are entering the faith, so that those who come may deliberate, those who observe it may persevere, and those who do not observe it may renounce themselves.

For we shall see whether, according to the type of the ark, the raven and the kite and the wolf and the dog and the serpent will be in the church. Certainly the idolater is not found in the type of the ark. No animal was figured as an idolater. What was not in the ark should not be in the church.

problems.quote: Every wave of it chokes them; every whirlpool of it sucks them down to the dead.
problems.source_quote: quicumque fluctus eius offocant, omnis uertex eius ad inferos desorbet.
problems.why: Latin says those who choke the waves cause the whole to sink; English reverses who is choking whom.
problems.fix: Whoever smothers its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.
problems.ruling: quicumque fluctus eius offocant = 'whoever its waves choke'; English reverses agency, making waves the subject instead of the choked victims.

edits.old: Every wave of it chokes them; every whirlpool of it sucks them down to the dead.
edits.new: Whoever smothers its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.

fixed: Agency reversed: source 'quicumque fluctus eius offocant, omnis uertex eius ad inferos desorbet' means whoever chokes its waves, the whole of it sinks to the underworld; English had the waves choking them.

problems.quote: But for those who are thrown out, the deep cannot be swum; for those who run aground, the shipwreck cannot be escaped; for those who are swallowed down, the drowning in idolatry leaves no breath.
problems.source_quote: ceterum inenatabile excussis profundum est, inextricabile inpactis naufragium est, inrespirabile deuoratis hypobrychium in idololatria.
problems.why: English adds agency and changes meaning; source describes the deep, shipwreck, drowning as inexorable, not about people being thrown out.
problems.fix: The deep is inexorable when struck, the shipwreck is inextricable when impacted, and the drowning in idolatry is breathless.
problems.ruling: 'excussis' = shaken/cast out persons; 'inenatabile' = unswimmable. Translation conveys source meaning adequately, not a major error.

edits.old: But for those who are thrown out, the deep cannot be swum; for those who run aground, the shipwreck cannot be escaped; for those who are swallowed down, the drowning in idolatry leaves no breath.
edits.new: But the deep is unswimmable for those who are shaken out; the shipwreck is inextricable for those who are driven upon them; the drowning in idolatry is unbreathable for those who are swallowed down.

fixed: The English added agency and changed the meaning; the source describes the deep, shipwreck, and drowning as inexorable conditions, not actions done to people. The edit restores the source's structure while keeping the English natural.

problems.why: attonita means astonished or stunned, not thunderstruck; the translation alters the condition of security

edits.new: secure even if it is astonished

fixed: Changed 'secure if it is thunderstruck' to 'secure even if it is astonished' because attonita means astonished or stunned, not thunderstruck, and the condition of security is altered by the mistranslation.

problems.why: Same concept (non-Christians) rendered as 'nations,' 'pagans,' and 'outsiders' interchangeably.
problems.fix: Use 'pagans' consistently or note that 'nations' = pagans.

problems.quote: Whoever smothers its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.
problems.why: Subject-verb relation is broken; 'whoever smothers' does not connect to 'the whole of it sinks.'
problems.fix: Restructure: 'Whoever is overwhelmed by its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.'

edits.old: Whoever smothers its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.
edits.new: Whoever is overwhelmed by its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.

fixed: Glossary issue: 'the nations' does not appear in the current English; the text uses 'pagans' consistently, so no edit is needed.

Unreadable: The source reads 'quicumque fluctus eius offocant, omnis uertex eius ad inferos desorbet' — 'all its waves choke them; every whirlpool of it sucks them down to the dead.' The English 'Whoever smothers its waves' misstates the subject; corrected to 'Whoever is overwhelmed by its waves' to restore the passive sense of being choked by the waves.

last_rejected.quote: secure even if it is astonished
last_rejected.why: 'Attonita' means 'stunned/struck' by fear, not 'astonished'; the contrast is safe-if-careful vs. secure-even-if-terrified.
last_rejected.fix: secure even if it is struck with dread
last_rejected.ruling: attonita = astonished/stunned; translation matches acceptable sense, not a meaning change

last_rejected.quote: Whoever smothers its waves, the whole of it sinks down to the underworld.
last_rejected.source_quote: quicumque fluctus eius offocant, omnis uertex eius ad inferos desorbet
last_rejected.why: 'Offocant' = choke/smother; 'uertex' = whirlpool, not 'the whole of it.' The whirlpool sucks down to the underworld.
last_rejected.fix: Whoever its waves choke, every whirlpool of it sucks down to the underworld.
last_rejected.ruling: vertex = whirl/vortex; translation vague but overall sense unchanged, not a major error

polish.changed: Clarified the shipwreck imagery by making each subject explicit, smoothed the sentence rhythm for reading aloud, and kept every claim and qualification intact.
